scientific_vocabulary.definition: Substances that undergo chemical change in a chemical reaction.
scientific_vocabulary.usage_context: Written on the left-hand side (LHS) of a chemical equation.

scientific_vocabulary.definition: New substances formed during a chemical reaction.
scientific_vocabulary.usage_context: Written on the right-hand side (RHS) of a chemical equation.

scientific_vocabulary.definition: A chemical reaction in which heat/energy is released along with products.
scientific_vocabulary.usage_context: Respiration and burning of natural gas are exothermic.

scientific_vocabulary.definition: A chemical reaction in which energy is absorbed from surroundings.
scientific_vocabulary.usage_context: Thermal decomposition of calcium carbonate is endothermic.

scientific_vocabulary.definition: The slow degradation of metals due to reaction with atmospheric air, moisture, or chemicals.
scientific_vocabulary.usage_context: Rusting of iron forming hydrated ferric oxide (2Fe2O3.xH2O).

scientific_vocabulary.definition: The oxidation of fats and oils in food resulting in unpleasant taste and odor.
scientific_vocabulary.usage_context: Prevented by packing potato chips with nitrogen gas.

scientific_vocabulary.definition: A chemical substance that changes color or odor in acidic or basic media.
scientific_vocabulary.usage_context: Litmus paper, phenolphthalein, and methyl orange.

scientific_vocabulary.definition: A numerical scale ranging from 0 to 14 measuring hydrogen ion concentration in solution.
scientific_vocabulary.usage_context: pH < 7 is acidic, pH = 7 is neutral, pH > 7 is basic.

scientific_vocabulary.definition: Metal oxides that react with both acids and bases to produce salt and water.
scientific_vocabulary.usage_context: Aluminium oxide (Al2O3) and Zinc oxide (ZnO).

scientific_vocabulary.definition: Heating sulphide ores strongly in the presence of excess air to convert them into metal oxides.
scientific_vocabulary.usage_context: 2ZnS + 3O2 -> 2ZnO + 2SO2.

scientific_vocabulary.definition: Heating carbonate ores strongly in limited or absent air to convert them into metal oxides.
scientific_vocabulary.usage_context: ZnCO3 -> ZnO + CO2.

scientific_vocabulary.definition: The unique property of carbon atoms to form strong covalent bonds with other carbon atoms, forming long chains or rings.
scientific_vocabulary.usage_context: Enables formation of millions of organic compounds.

scientific_vocabulary.definition: A family of organic compounds sharing the same functional group and chemical properties, where successive members differ by -CH2-.
scientific_vocabulary.usage_context: Alkanes (CnH2n+2): Methane, Ethane, Propane, Butane.

scientific_vocabulary.definition: A spherical aggregate of soap molecules in water where hydrophobic tails point inward and hydrophilic heads face outward.
scientific_vocabulary.usage_context: Traps oily dirt at its core during cleansing action of soap.

scientific_vocabulary.definition: The loss of water in the form of vapor from aerial parts of a plant (stomata).
scientific_vocabulary.usage_context: Creates suction pull for upward transport of water and minerals in xylem.

scientific_vocabulary.definition: The transport of soluble products of photosynthesis (sucrose) through phloem tissue using energy (ATP).
scientific_vocabulary.usage_context: Moves food from leaves to storage organs and growing tips.

scientific_vocabulary.definition: The fundamental structural and functional filtration unit of the human kidney.
scientific_vocabulary.usage_context: Filters metabolic urea and uric acid from blood.

scientific_vocabulary.definition: The microscopic chemical junction between the axon terminal of one neuron and the dendrite of the next.
scientific_vocabulary.usage_context: Transmits nerve signals via chemical neurotransmitters.

scientific_vocabulary.definition: The rapid neural pathway that controls an automatic, involuntary reflex action in response to a stimulus.
scientific_vocabulary.usage_context: Receptor -> Sensory neuron -> Spinal cord -> Motor neuron -> Effector muscle.

scientific_vocabulary.definition: A specialized disc-like vascular tissue connecting the embryo to the uterine wall.
scientific_vocabulary.usage_context: Supplies glucose and oxygen to fetus and removes metabolic wastes.

scientific_vocabulary.definition: The ratio of the speed of light in vacuum (c) to the speed of light in a medium (v).
scientific_vocabulary.usage_context: n = c / v. Measures optical density of a medium.

scientific_vocabulary.definition: The degree of convergence or divergence of light rays achieved by a lens, defined as reciprocal of focal length in meters.
scientific_vocabulary.usage_context: P = 1 / f (in meters). SI unit: Dioptre (D).

scientific_vocabulary.definition: The splitting of white light into its seven constituent colors (VIBGYOR) when passing through a refracting medium like a glass prism.
scientific_vocabulary.usage_context: Occurs because different wavelengths bend at different angles.
scientific_vocabulary.source_reference: Chapter 10: The Human Eye and the Colourful World

scientific_vocabulary.definition: An intrinsic property of a conductor measuring its opposition to electric current per unit length and cross-sectional area.
scientific_vocabulary.usage_context: R = ρ * (L / A). SI unit: Ohm-meter (Ω·m).

scientific_vocabulary.definition: The progressive accumulation of non-biodegradable toxic chemicals at higher concentrations at successive trophic levels.
scientific_vocabulary.usage_context: DDT concentration increases from plankton to apex birds/humans.

definitions.definition: A process in which one or more substances undergo chemical transformation to form new substances with entirely different physical and chemical properties.
A chemical equation in which the total number of atoms of each element is equal on both the reactant and product sides.
A reaction in which two or more reactants combine to form a single product.
A reaction in which a single compound breaks down into two or more simpler substances upon heating, light exposure, or electricity.
A chemical reaction in which a more reactive element displaces a less reactive element from its salt solution.
A reaction in which there is an exchange of ions between two reactant compounds to form two new compounds.
A reaction in which one reactant undergoes oxidation (gains oxygen / loses electrons) while another undergoes reduction (loses oxygen / gains electrons) simultaneously.
A substance that produces hydrogen ions [H+] or hydronium ions [H3O+] in aqueous solution, tastes sour, and turns blue litmus paper red.
A substance that produces hydroxide ions [OH-] in aqueous solution, tastes bitter, feels soapy, and turns red litmus paper blue.
The chemical reaction between an acid and a base to produce salt and water.
The fixed number of water molecules present in one formula unit of a salt crystal.
The scientific process of extracting metals from their ores and refining them for practical use.
The phenomenon where compounds possess identical molecular formulas but different structural arrangements of carbon atoms.
The biochemical process by which autotrophic green plants synthesize glucose from carbon dioxide and water in the presence of sunlight and chlorophyll.
The cellular process of breaking down nutrient molecules (glucose) to release bioavailable energy in the form of ATP.
A circulatory pattern in which blood passes through the heart twice during each complete circuit of the body (pulmonary and systemic loops).
The biological process of removing toxic metabolic waste products (urea, uric acid) from the body.
Chemical messengers synthesized naturally by plants that regulate growth, development, and environmental responses.
The directional growth movement of a plant part in response to light stimulus.
An asexual mode of reproduction where new plants develop from vegetative parts (root, stem, leaf) of parent plants.
The structural and functional unit of heredity composed of a specific DNA segment coding for a protein or physical trait.
1. The angle of incidence equals the angle of reflection (i = r). 2. The incident ray, reflected ray, and normal at the point of incidence all lie in the same plane.
The ratio of the sine of the angle of incidence to the sine of the angle of refraction is constant for a given pair of media and light wavelength.
The ability of the human eye crystalline lens to adjust its focal length using ciliary muscles to focus objects at varying distances clearly.

definitions.definition: At constant temperature, the electric current flowing through a conductor is directly proportional to the potential difference across its ends (V = I * R).
The heat produced in a resistor is directly proportional to the square of current, resistance, and time of current flow (H = I^2 * R * t).
A long coil of insulated copper wire consisting of many closely wound circular turns that produces a uniform interior magnetic field when electric current passes through it.
definitions.source_reference: Chapter 12: Magnetic Effects of Electric Current

definitions.definition: A self-sustaining biological community where living organisms (biotic) interact with each other and their non-living physical environment (abiotic).

concepts.concept_name: Balancing Chemical Equations via Mass Conservation
concepts.explanation: Mass cannot be created or destroyed in a chemical reaction. Therefore, the total mass of products must equal the total mass of reactants, requiring an identical count of each element's atoms on both sides of the equation.
The pH of a solution is inversely proportional to its hydrogen ion [H+] concentration. Solutions with pH < 7 are acidic (higher H+), pH = 7 is neutral, and pH > 7 is basic (higher OH-).
Metals are arranged in decreasing order of their chemical reactivity. Highly reactive metals (K, Na, Ca) displace less reactive metals (Cu, Ag) from their aqueous salt solutions.

concepts.concept_name: Covalent Bonding and Octet Completion in Carbon
concepts.explanation: Carbon has 4 valence electrons. Instead of forming C4+ or C4- ions (which require excessive energy), carbon shares 4 pairs of electrons with other atoms to complete its octet via stable covalent bonds.

Glucose (6-carbon) splits into Pyruvate (3-carbon) in the cytoplasm. In mitochondria with O2, it yields CO2, H2O, and 38 ATP. In yeast without O2, it yields ethanol, CO2, and 2 ATP. In human muscle under O2 deficit, it yields lactic acid and 2 ATP.

Nervous coordination uses electrical impulses along neurons for rapid, point-to-point, short-lived responses. Hormonal coordination uses chemical messengers (hormones) in blood for widespread, sustained physiological growth and regulation.

concepts.concept_name: DNA Replication and Variation in Reproduction
concepts.explanation: DNA copying during reproduction creates cellular apparatus for offspring. Inaccuracies in biochemical DNA copying introduce variations essential for species adaptation and evolutionary survival under changing niches.
concepts.source_reference: Chapter 7 & 8: How do Organisms Reproduce? & Heredity

concepts.explanation: Traits are inherited as discrete gene pairs (alleles). Dominant alleles (T) express their phenotype in both homozygous (TT) and heterozygous (Tt) states, while recessive alleles (t) express only in homozygous (tt) state.

When light passes obliquely from one medium to another, its speed changes due to differing optical densities, causing the light ray to bend towards the normal (rarer to denser) or away from the normal (denser to rarer).

Light rays passing through atmospheric air layers of continuously changing optical density undergo continuous refraction, causing star twinkling, apparent star elevation, and advanced sunrise / delayed sunset.
concepts.source_reference: Chapter 10: The Human Eye and the Colourful World

concepts.explanation: In series, current is constant across all resistors and equivalent resistance Rs = R1 + R2 + R3. In parallel, voltage is constant across all branches and equivalent resistance 1/Rp = 1/R1 + 1/R2 + 1/R3.

A current-carrying wire produces a magnetic field (Right-Hand Thumb Rule). Placing it in an external magnetic field creates a mechanical force (Fleming's Left-Hand Rule), which drives electric motors.
concepts.source_reference: Chapter 12: Magnetic Effects of Electric Current

concepts.concept_name: Energy Flow and 10% Law in Ecosystems
concepts.explanation: Energy flow through an ecosystem is unidirectional. According to Lindeman's 10% Law, only 10% of energy at one trophic level is transferred to the next, limiting food chains to 3-4 steps.

principles_laws.name: Law of Conservation of Mass
principles_laws.statement: Mass can neither be created nor destroyed in a chemical reaction; the total mass of products equals the total mass of reactants.
principles_laws.variables_or_terms: Sum of Reactant Masses = Sum of Product Masses

principles_laws.name: Law of Conservation of Energy
principles_laws.statement: Energy can neither be created nor destroyed; it can only be transformed from one form to another.

principles_laws.name: Mendel's Law of Segregation
principles_laws.statement: Allele pairs segregate independently during gamete formation so that each gamete carries only one allele for each gene.
principles_laws.variables_or_terms: Monohybrid Cross Phenotypic Ratio = 3:1, Genotypic Ratio = 1:2:1

principles_laws.name: Mendel's Law of Independent Assortment
principles_laws.statement: Alleles of two different genes segregate independently of each other during gamete formation.

principles_laws.name: Law of Reflection
principles_laws.statement: 1. Angle of incidence equals angle of reflection (i = r). 2. Incident ray, reflected ray, and normal lie in the same plane.

principles_laws.name: Snell's Law of Refraction
principles_laws.statement: The ratio of sine of angle of incidence to sine of angle of refraction is constant for a given pair of media.
principles_laws.variables_or_terms: sin i / sin r = n21 = v1 / v2

principles_laws.name: Ohm's Law
principles_laws.statement: Electric current flowing through a conductor is directly proportional to potential difference across its ends at constant temperature.

principles_laws.name: Joule's Law of Heating
principles_laws.statement: Heat produced in a resistor is directly proportional to the square of current, resistance, and time.

principles_laws.name: Right-Hand Thumb Rule
principles_laws.statement: If a current-carrying straight conductor is held in the right hand with thumb pointing along current direction, curled fingers show magnetic field line direction.
principles_laws.variables_or_terms: Thumb = Current, Curled Fingers = Magnetic Field Lines
principles_laws.source_reference: Chapter 12: Magnetic Effects of Electric Current

principles_laws.name: Fleming's Left-Hand Rule
principles_laws.statement: Stretch Forefinger, Middle finger, and Thumb of left hand mutually perpendicular: Forefinger = Magnetic Field, Middle finger = Current, Thumb = Mechanical Force/Motion.
principles_laws.variables_or_terms: Forefinger = B, Middle finger = I, Thumb = F
principles_laws.source_reference: Chapter 12: Magnetic Effects of Electric Current

principles_laws.name: Lindeman's 10% Energy Transfer Law
principles_laws.statement: Only 10% of the energy stored in biomass at one trophic level is passed on to the next higher trophic level.

principles_laws.name: Rayleigh Scattering Law
principles_laws.statement: The intensity of scattered light is inversely proportional to the fourth power of its wavelength.
principles_laws.source_reference: Chapter 10: The Human Eye and the Colourful World

steps: Pass electric current through acidulated water in an electrolytic cell.
Water molecules decompose into hydrogen and oxygen gases.
Hydrogen gas evolves at the Cathode (-) and Oxygen gas evolves at the Anode (+).
Balanced Equation: 2H2O(l) -> 2H2(g) + O2(g) (2:1 volume ratio).
Pass electricity through aqueous sodium chloride solution (brine).
Brine decomposes into Sodium Hydroxide (NaOH), Chlorine gas (Cl2), and Hydrogen gas (H2).
Chlorine gas is released at Anode (+); Hydrogen gas at Cathode (-); NaOH solution collects near Cathode.
Balanced Equation: 2NaCl(aq) + 2H2O(l) -> 2NaOH(aq) + Cl2(g) + H2(g).
Set up cell with impure copper block as Anode, pure copper sheet as Cathode, and acidified CuSO4 solution as Electrolyte.
Pass electric current through the cell.
Pure Cu from anode dissolves into electrolyte solution as Cu2+ ions.
Equivalent pure Cu2+ ions deposit from solution onto the cathode.
Insoluble impurities settle below anode as Anode Mud.
Esterification: Heat Ethanoic acid with Ethanol in presence of concentrated H2SO4 catalyst to form sweet-smelling Ethyl ethanoate ester (CH3COOH + C2H5OH -> CH3COOC2H5 + H2O).
Saponification: Heat ester with NaOH alkali to convert it back into Sodium ethanoate soap and Ethanol (CH3COOC2H5 + NaOH -> CH3COONa + C2H5OH).
Chlorophyll absorbs light solar energy in chloroplasts.
Light energy splits water molecules (H2O) into Hydrogen and Oxygen gas.
Carbon dioxide (CO2) is reduced into glucose carbohydrates (C6H12O6).
Overall Equation: 6CO2 + 12H2O --(Sunlight/Chlorophyll)--> C6H12O6 + 6O2 + 6H2O.
Deoxygenated blood from body enters Right Atrium -> Right Ventricle -> pumped via Pulmonary Artery to Lungs.
Blood absorbs O2 in lungs and returns via Pulmonary Veins to Left Atrium.
Oxygenated blood moves to Left Ventricle -> pumped via Aorta to entire body.
Passes through heart twice per complete body circuit, ensuring complete separation of O2 and CO2 blood.
Glomerular Ultrafiltration: Blood pressure filters water, glucose, amino acids, salts, and urea from glomerulus into Bowman's capsule.
Tubular Selective Reabsorption: Useful glucose, amino acids, salts, and water are reabsorbed into surrounding blood capillaries along renal tubule.
Tubular Secretion & Collection: Nitrogenous wastes (urea) pass into collecting duct as concentrated urine.
Receptor cell in sense organ (skin) detects stimulus (heat/pain).
Sensory neuron transmits electrical impulse to Spinal Cord.
Relay neuron in spinal cord processes signal and triggers Motor neuron instantly.
Motor neuron signals Effector muscle to contract, pulling limb away from danger.
Light strikes plant shoot tip from one side.
Auxin hormone synthesized at shoot tip diffuses to the shaded side.
Higher auxin concentration on shaded side stimulates faster cell elongation.
Unequal elongation causes the stem tip to bend towards the light source.
Pollen tube grows down style into ovary and enters ovule.
Syngamy: 1st male gamete fuses with egg cell to form diploid Zygote.
Triple Fusion: 2nd male gamete fuses with 2 polar nuclei to form triploid Endosperm.
Post-fertilization: Zygote becomes Embryo, Ovule becomes Seed, Ovary matures into Fruit.
Sunlight enters atmospheric raindrop and refracts/disperses into constituent colors.
Dispersed rays undergo Total Internal Reflection at inner back wall of raindrop.
Rays refract again as they exit front face of raindrop into air, projecting colorful spectrum arc.
processes.source_reference: Chapter 10: The Human Eye and the Colourful World

processes.process_name: Stratospheric Ozone Formation and CFC Depletion
steps: Ozone Formation: Solar UV radiation splits O2 molecules into free O atoms (O2 --UV--> O + O); free O atom combines with O2 to form Ozone (O + O2 -> O3).
CFC Depletion: Chlorofluorocarbons rise to stratosphere where UV releases free chlorine radicals; chlorine catalyzes destruction of O3 into O2.

structures_functions.description: Microscopic pores located on leaf epidermis flanked by two kidney-shaped Guard Cells.
structures_functions.function: Guard cells swell/shrink with water to open/close stomatal pore for gas exchange (CO2/O2) and transpiration water loss.

structures_functions.description: Muscular organ comprising two upper Atria, two lower Ventricles, and a central muscular Septum.
structures_functions.function: Septum completely separates oxygenated and deoxygenated blood streams, enabling high energy efficiency in warm-blooded humans.

structures_functions.description: Cup-like sack (Bowman's capsule) enclosing a dense capillary network (Glomerulus).
structures_functions.function: Filters blood under high pressure to separate nitrogenous waste (urea), glucose, and salts from blood cells.

structures_functions.description: Cell body (cyton) with branched dendrites, a long axon coated in myelin sheath, and terminal nerve endings.
structures_functions.function: Dendrites acquire stimuli; axon transmits electrical nerve impulses to synaptic terminal for chemical signal transmission.

structures_functions.description: Disc-shaped vascular structure embedded in uterine wall containing fetal villi surrounded by maternal blood spaces.
structures_functions.function: Facilitates diffusion of oxygen, glucose, and nutrients from mother to fetus and eliminates fetal urea and CO2 into maternal blood.

structures_functions.description: Spherical cluster of soap molecules with ionic heads (-COONa) on outer surface and hydrocarbon tails pointing inward.
structures_functions.function: Emulsifies oily dirt at its hydrophobic core, allowing grease to be rinsed away in water.

structures_functions.description: Circular ring of smooth muscle tissue surrounding the crystalline eye lens.
structures_functions.function: Relaxes to flatten lens for distant vision (focal length increases) and contracts to thicken lens for near vision (focal length decreases).
structures_functions.source_reference: Chapter 10: The Human Eye and the Colourful World

structures_functions.description: Two half-ring copper metallic segments P and Q attached to rotating axle of motor armature coil.
structures_functions.function: Reverses electric current direction in armature coil every half rotation to sustain continuous uni-directional torque.
structures_functions.source_reference: Chapter 12: Magnetic Effects of Electric Current

structures_functions.description: Helical cylinder composed of many tightly wound turns of insulated copper wire.
structures_functions.function: Generates a uniform interior magnetic field identical to a bar magnet when connected to a DC power supply.
structures_functions.source_reference: Chapter 12: Magnetic Effects of Electric Current

structures_functions.description: Green-insulated copper wire connected from metal appliance casing directly to a metal plate buried deep in earth.
structures_functions.function: Provides a low-resistance safety grounding path for leakage current, preventing severe electric shocks to users.
structures_functions.source_reference: Chapter 12: Magnetic Effects of Electric Current

types_or_branches: Natural Indicators (Litmus, Turmeric, Red Cabbage extract)
High Reactivity Metals (K, Na, Ca, Mg, Al) -> Electrolysis of molten chloride/oxide
Moderate Reactivity Metals (Zn, Fe, Pb, Cu) -> Roasting/Calcination followed by Carbon reduction
Low Reactivity Metals (Hg, Ag, Au) -> Native state or simple heating of sulphide ore
Saturated Hydrocarbons (Alkanes, single C-C bond, general formula CnH2n+2)
Unsaturated Hydrocarbons - Alkenes (double C=C bond, general formula CnH2n)
Unsaturated Hydrocarbons - Alkynes (triple C≡C bond, general formula CnH2n-2)
Saprotrophic Nutrition (fungi, bread mould - digest food externally)
Parasitic Nutrition (cuscuta, ticks, tapeworms - derive nourishment without killing host)
Holozoic Nutrition (amoeba, humans - ingest solid organic matter digested internally)
Vegetative Propagation (Cutting, Layering, Grafting in Rose, Bryophyllum leaf buds)
Presbyopia (Old age accommodation loss) -> Corrected by Bifocal lens
Cataract (Clouding of crystalline lens) -> Corrected by Cataract surgery
classifications.source_reference: Chapter 10: The Human Eye and the Colourful World

types_or_branches: Biodegradable Waste (vegetable peels, paper, dung - broken down by biological decomposers)
Non-Biodegradable Waste (plastics, glass, DDT - persist without enzymatic breakdown)

cause_effect.cause: Burning magnesium ribbon in presence of atmospheric oxygen
cause_effect.effect: Forms white Magnesium Oxide (MgO) powder with a dazzling white flame.

cause_effect.cause: Immersing an iron nail into blue copper sulphate solution
cause_effect.effect: Iron displaces copper, turning solution pale green (FeSO4) and depositing reddish-brown copper on nail.

cause_effect.cause: Mouth pH falling below 5.5 due to bacterial sugar fermentation
cause_effect.effect: Corrodes tooth enamel (calcium hydroxyapatite), initiating tooth decay.

cause_effect.cause: Lack of oxygen during intense muscle exercise
cause_effect.effect: Pyruvate breaks down anaerobically into Lactic Acid, causing severe muscle cramps.

cause_effect.cause: Unidirectional light shining on a plant shoot tip
cause_effect.effect: Auxin diffuses to shaded side stimulating cell elongation, bending shoot tip toward light (phototropism).

cause_effect.cause: Elongated eyeball or excessive eye lens curvature
cause_effect.effect: Parallel rays focus in front of retina, resulting in Myopia (near-sightedness).
cause_effect.source_reference: Chapter 10: The Human Eye and the Colourful World

cause_effect.cause: Shortened eyeball or excessive focal length of eye lens
cause_effect.effect: Near rays focus behind retina, resulting in Hypermetropia (far-sightedness).
cause_effect.source_reference: Chapter 10: The Human Eye and the Colourful World

cause_effect.cause: Atmospheric refraction through turbulent air layers of changing temperature
cause_effect.effect: Apparent position of stars fluctuates continuously, causing twinkling of stars.
cause_effect.source_reference: Chapter 10: The Human Eye and the Colourful World

cause_effect.cause: Rayleigh scattering of short blue wavelengths by fine atmospheric air molecules
cause_effect.effect: Clear daytime sky appears blue to observers on Earth.
cause_effect.source_reference: Chapter 10: The Human Eye and the Colourful World

cause_effect.cause: Excessive electric current passing through circuit wiring
cause_effect.effect: Joule heating (I^2Rt) melts fuse wire, opening circuit and preventing electrical fires.

cause_effect.cause: Release of Chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs) into upper atmosphere
cause_effect.effect: Free chlorine atoms catalyze destruction of stratospheric ozone layer, opening ozone holes.

cause_effect.cause: Non-biodegradable pesticides (DDT) entering soil and aquatic food chains
cause_effect.effect: Progressive accumulation at higher trophic levels (Biological Magnification), reaching maximum toxicity in humans.

observations.observation: Magnesium ribbon burns with a dazzling white flame to form a white powder of Magnesium Oxide (MgO).
observations.inference: Magnesium combines with atmospheric oxygen in an exothermic combination reaction: 2Mg + O2 -> 2MgO.

observations.observation: During electrolysis of water, the volume of gas collected at the cathode is double the volume collected at the anode.
observations.inference: Water consists of 2 hydrogen atoms to 1 oxygen atom. Hydrogen gas evolves at Cathode (-) and Oxygen gas at Anode (+).

observations.observation: Zinc granules added to dilute H2SO4 produce gas bubbles that burn with a pop sound when tested with a burning candle.
observations.inference: Metals react with dilute acids to evolve flammable Hydrogen gas: Zn + H2SO4 -> ZnSO4 + H2.

observations.observation: An iron nail immersed in blue CuSO4 solution turns the solution pale green while a reddish-brown coating forms on the nail.
observations.inference: Iron is more reactive than copper and displaces Cu to form ferrous sulphate (FeSO4): Fe + CuSO4 -> FeSO4 + Cu.

observations.observation: Warming ethanol and ethanoic acid with concentrated H2SO4 produces a pleasant, sweet, fruity smell.
observations.inference: Carboxylic acids react with alcohols under acid catalysis to produce sweet-smelling Esters (Ethyl ethanoate).

observations.observation: When a destarched variegated leaf exposed to sunlight is decolorized and treated with iodine, only green patches turn blue-black.
observations.inference: Chlorophyll is essential for photosynthesis and starch synthesis in green plant tissue.

observations.observation: A potted plant seedling kept in a dark box receiving light from a side window bends its shoot towards the window light.
observations.inference: Auxin hormone diffuses to the shaded side, stimulating cell elongation and positive phototropism.

observations.observation: Yeast suspension in sugar solution observed under a microscope shows small protuberances forming chains of buds.
observations.inference: Yeast reproduces rapidly by an asexual mode called Budding.

observations.observation: Light entering a rectangular glass slab emerges parallel to the incident ray but shifted laterally.
observations.inference: Bending at the air-glass interface is equal and opposite to bending at the glass-air interface (Angle i = Angle e).

observations.observation: Passing a white light spectrum through an identical inverted second glass prism recombines the spectrum into a white light beam.
observations.inference: Prisms disperse white light based on refractive index differences; dispersion is fully reversible.
observations.source_reference: Chapter 10: The Human Eye and the Colourful World

observations.observation: Plotting potential difference (V) against current (I) for a nichrome wire yields a straight line passing through the origin.
observations.inference: Current is directly proportional to potential difference (V ∝ I), verifying Ohm's Law.

observations.observation: Iron filings sprinkled around a bar magnet arrange themselves in continuous curved lines emerging from N pole and entering S pole.
observations.inference: Maps the magnetic field line pattern around a bar magnet, demonstrating field strength maximum near poles.
observations.source_reference: Chapter 12: Magnetic Effects of Electric Current

observations.observation: Vegetable peels buried in soil decompose into dark compost within 3 weeks, while buried plastic bags remain unchanged.
observations.inference: Bacterial decomposers break down natural organic matter but lack enzymes to digest synthetic non-biodegradable polymers.

experiments_activities.objective: To demonstrate a chemical combination reaction and observe oxide formation.
experiments_activities.materials: Magnesium ribbon (3-4 cm), Sandpaper, Tongs, Spirit lamp/Burner, Watch glass
procedure: Clean a 3-4 cm long magnesium ribbon with sandpaper to remove protective oxide layer.
Hold the ribbon with tongs and burn it using a spirit lamp.
Collect the white ash formed in a watch glass.
experiments_activities.observation: Magnesium burns with a dazzling white flame, producing a white powder of Magnesium Oxide.
experiments_activities.conclusion: Magnesium reacts with oxygen to form Magnesium Oxide: 2Mg(s) + O2(g) -> 2MgO(s).

experiments_activities.objective: To observe electrolytic decomposition of water into hydrogen and oxygen.
experiments_activities.materials: Plastic mug, Carbon graphite rods, 6V Battery, Rubber stoppers, Test tubes, Dilute H2SO4
procedure: Drill two holes at base of plastic mug, fit rubber stoppers, and insert carbon electrodes.
Fill mug with water and add drops of dilute H2SO4 to increase conductivity.
Invert two water-filled test tubes over electrodes and connect to 6V battery.
experiments_activities.observation: Gas bubbles form at both electrodes. Hydrogen volume at Cathode (-) is double the Oxygen volume at Anode (+).

experiments_activities.activity_title: Activity 2.3: Action of Acids on Metals
experiments_activities.objective: To test gas evolved during metal-acid reaction.
experiments_activities.materials: Zinc granules, Dilute H2SO4, Test tube, Delivery tube, Soap solution, Burning candle
procedure: Take 5 mL dilute H2SO4 in test tube and add zinc granules.
Pass evolved gas through soap solution in a trough.
Bring a burning candle near gas-filled soap bubbles.
experiments_activities.observation: Soap bubbles rise and burn with a characteristic 'pop' sound when touched by candle flame.
experiments_activities.conclusion: Zinc displaces hydrogen from acid releasing flammable H2 gas: Zn + H2SO4 -> ZnSO4 + H2.

experiments_activities.objective: To compare reactivity of Iron and Copper.
experiments_activities.materials: Iron nails, Copper sulphate solution, Test tubes, Sandpaper, Thread
procedure: Clean iron nails with sandpaper.
Immerse iron nail in 10 mL blue CuSO4 solution in a test tube for 20 minutes.
Compare color change of solution and nail with a control setup.
experiments_activities.observation: Blue CuSO4 solution turns pale green (FeSO4); reddish-brown copper deposits on iron nail.
experiments_activities.conclusion: Iron is more reactive than copper: Fe(s) + CuSO4(aq) -> FeSO4(aq) + Cu(s).

experiments_activities.objective: To synthesize an ester from ethanol and ethanoic acid.
experiments_activities.materials: 1 mL Ethanol, 1 mL Glacial ethanoic acid, Conc. H2SO4, Test tube, Beaker, Water bath
procedure: Mix 1 mL ethanol and 1 mL ethanoic acid with 3-4 drops of conc. H2SO4 in a test tube.
Warm in a water bath for 5 minutes.
Pour contents into a beaker containing 20 mL water and smell.
experiments_activities.observation: A sweet, fruity aroma is detected.
experiments_activities.conclusion: Acid-catalysed reaction forms Ethyl ethanoate ester: CH3COOH + C2H5OH -> CH3COOC2H5 + H2O.

experiments_activities.objective: To prove chlorophyll is necessary for photosynthesis.
experiments_activities.materials: Potted plant with variegated leaves (Money plant), Alcohol, Water bath, Iodine solution
procedure: Destarch potted plant in dark room for 3 days.
Expose to sunlight for 6 hours.
Trace variegated leaf green areas on paper.
Boil leaf in alcohol to decolorize, then dip in iodine solution.
experiments_activities.observation: Only leaf regions that were previously green turn blue-black with iodine.
experiments_activities.conclusion: Chlorophyll is essential for starch synthesis during photosynthesis.

experiments_activities.objective: To observe shoot tropism towards light.
experiments_activities.materials: Conical flask, Plant seedling, Cardboard box with side window, Light source
procedure: Place a seedling flask inside a dark box with light entering from one side window.
Observe shoot direction after 3-4 days.
experiments_activities.observation: Plant shoot bends towards the light window.
experiments_activities.conclusion: Auxin stimulates cell elongation on shaded side, causing positive phototropism.

experiments_activities.activity_title: Activity 9.10: Glass Slab Refraction and Lateral Displacement
experiments_activities.objective: To verify Snell's Law and measure lateral shift.
experiments_activities.materials: Rectangular glass slab, Drawing board, Drawing pins, Protractor, Ruler
procedure: Fix white paper on drawing board and place glass slab.
Insert two pins along incident ray at angle i.
Fix two pins on opposite side aligning with pin images.
Draw incident, refracted, and emergent rays.
experiments_activities.observation: Emergent ray is parallel to incident ray but displaced laterally (Angle i = Angle e).
experiments_activities.conclusion: Light bends towards normal entering glass and away from normal entering air.

experiments_activities.objective: To determine V-I relationship and calculate resistance.
experiments_activities.materials: Nichrome wire, Ammeter, Voltmeter, 4 Dry cells (1.5V each), Plug key
procedure: Connect circuit with 1 cell; record V across wire and current I.
Repeat by connecting 2, 3, and 4 cells in series.
Plot V vs I graph.
experiments_activities.observation: V-I plot is a straight line passing through origin; ratio V/I is constant.
experiments_activities.conclusion: Current is directly proportional to potential difference (V = I * R).

experiments_activities.activity_title: Activity 12.2: Magnetic Field Pattern of Bar Magnet
experiments_activities.objective: To map magnetic field lines around a bar magnet.
experiments_activities.materials: Bar magnet, Cardboard, Iron filings, Salt shaker
procedure: Place bar magnet on cardboard.
Sprinkle iron filings uniformly using shaker.
Tap cardboard gently.
experiments_activities.observation: Iron filings arrange in continuous curved lines emerging from N pole and entering S pole.
experiments_activities.conclusion: Visualizes magnetic field lines showing high field intensity near poles.
experiments_activities.source_reference: Chapter 12: Magnetic Effects of Electric Current

applications.description: Antacids like Baking Soda (NaHCO3) or Milk of Magnesia [Mg(OH)2] neutralise excess stomach acid (HCl). Quicklime (CaO) or slaked lime [Ca(OH)2] neutralises acidic agricultural soil to optimize crop yields.
Sodium hydroxide (NaOH) is used in soap/detergent manufacturing; Chlorine (Cl2) in water sterilization, PVC, and bleaching powder; Hydrogen (H2) in fuel cells and ammonia fertilizer synthesis.

applications.application_name: Plaster of Paris in Orthopedics and Architecture
applications.description: Plaster of Paris (CaSO4.1/2H2O) sets hard into Gypsum when mixed with water, used by doctors to immobilize fractured bones and by architects for decorative ceiling plaster.

applications.application_name: Thermit Reaction for Heavy Metal Welding
applications.description: Reduction of Iron(III) oxide with Aluminium powder releases molten iron (Fe2O3 + 2Al -> 2Fe + Al2O3 + Heat), used to weld cracked railway tracks and heavy machine frames in situ.
Galvanizing steel with a protective Zinc layer, anodizing aluminium, painting, greasing, and alloying (creating Stainless Steel with Cr and Ni) prevents rusting of vehicles, bridges, and cookware.
Unsaturated vegetable oils undergo addition reaction with H2 gas using Nickel catalyst to convert double bonds into saturated fats (vanaspati ghee).

applications.application_name: Cleansing Action of Soaps and Synthetic Detergents
applications.description: Micelles trap hydrophobic oil/grease droplets at their core while hydrophilic heads stay in water, emulsifying dirt so it washes away. Synthetic detergents clean effectively even in hard water without forming scum.
Hemodialysis machines pass patient blood through semi-permeable cellophan tubes bathed in dialysing fluid to remove toxic nitrogenous urea waste when kidneys fail.

Mechanical barriers (condoms) prevent unwanted pregnancies and block transmission of STDs (HIV-AIDS, Syphilis). Oral pills, Copper-T (IUCD), and surgical vasectomy/tubectomy provide reliable family planning.
Convex mirrors form erect, diminished, virtual images, offering drivers a significantly wider panoramic field of view behind the vehicle compared to plane mirrors.
Diverging Concave lenses correct Myopia by pushing image focus back onto retina. Converging Convex lenses correct Hypermetropia. Bifocal lenses correct Presbyopia.
applications.source_reference: Chapter 10: The Human Eye and the Colourful World

applications.application_name: Household Fuses and Earth Wire Grounding
applications.description: Electric fuse wire melts under excessive Joule heating (I^2Rt) to cut off overcurrent. Earth wire grounds metal appliance casings to prevent lethal electric shocks.
Electric motors convert electrical energy into mechanical rotational motion using split-ring commutators, powering washing machines, electric fans, ceiling fans, and water pumps.
applications.source_reference: Chapter 12: Magnetic Effects of Electric Current

applications.description: Two-bin segregation (Green wet bin for organic waste composting; Blue dry bin for plastic/glass recycling) minimizes landfill pollution and protects ecosystems.
